proposed_from.topic: Denominator-locked completeness for conditional causal effects in selected COPAGs. Fix a finite input-free COPAG over binary observed variables representing Chen--Mooij's positive discrete SCM class with arbitrary latent and selection variables, disjoint Y,X,C, and positive selected conditioning strata. Define Branch-sCIDP to enumerate every reachable role state using the source algorithm's current bucket intersections and valid Rule-2 exchanges, run sIDP on each terminal joint P(Y,Cbar | do(Xbar),S=1), and normalize any successful functional. Prove Branch-sCIDP succeeds iff P(Y | do(X),C,S=1) is identified; otherwise construct a denominator-locked selected conditional hedge: a represented MAG/sADMG and terminal-joint forest plus explicit positive rational binary SCMs with the same full selected observational law and the same positive conditioning denominator but different joint numerators. Give a shared-cache O(3^n poly(n)+output) formula-or-certificate algorithm and verification polynomial in graph plus expanded rational certificate size. Consumer: extend PAGId from no-selection conditional identification to formula-or-checkable-failure output for selected-cohort FCI/PAG analyses. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Varying one rational interior mechanism makes all fixed-regime masses affine; equality of the normalized selected observational law and conditioning denominator becomes a homogeneous rational system Av=0, while numerator disagreement is a row b outside row(A), so a locked witness exists exactly when rank([A;b]) exceeds rank(A). Exact enumeration produced a selected binary bow with identical observational laws, denominator 1/2, numerators 9/25 versus 7/23, and conditional effects 18/25 versus 14/23. It also verified both four-cycle graph realizations and exact cancellation of their conditional ratios. Checks corrected whole-bucket moves to role intersections, separated the independent-root cancellation model from the actual hedge realization, tested positivity and boundary cases, and found no current primary-source collision. These are derived special cases, not the complete converse. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that failure at every reachable terminal state forces a represented residual forest from which one can construct positive rational binary mechanisms sharing the selected observational law and conditioning denominator while separating the numerator, with the advertised output-sensitive synthesis bound. EARLY KILL TEST: Exhaustively enumerate input-free COPAGs on at most four observed vertices and their exact Rule-2 role-state graphs; any graph-valid identifying formula for an all-branches-fail conditional target refutes completeness, while a proof that all compatible rational binary pairs at a failing graph violate denominator locking refutes the certificate coordinate. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The two closest results are Chen--Mooij's sound selected conditional algorithm and complete unconditional selected-COPAG algorithm, and Duarte--Finkelstein--Knox--Mummolo--Shpitser's polynomial-program representation of discrete causal fibers. The strict new object is an exact denominator-locked certificate compiler: on a supplied rational interior affine SCM template it characterizes, by a simplex-tangent rank condition, whether the complete selected observational law and a positive selected conditioning denominator can be held fixed while the selected joint numerator changes. A connected positive rational binary example shows that the lock can hold by informative selection cancellation rather than because the conditioning variable is isolated; a same-graph perturbation shows that the equality is not graph-forced. No checked source subsumes this object. The proposal does not claim that every failed Branch-sCIDP instance supplies a passing direction; that residual-forest-to-rank implication is the first-class open question.

seed_details.kernel: Branch-sCIDP identifies \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X),C,S=\mathbf 1)\) if and only if the query is identified, and every failure yields a denominator-locked positive rational binary selected hedge.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The unconditional residual-forest construction must coordinate every reachable Rule-2 terminal state and preserve the terminal selected denominator.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for selected conditional hedge, denominator-locked hedge, and sCIDP completeness located no competing theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Chen--Mooij because sIDP is already complete.
seed_details.rebuttal: False: their paper expressly limits the completeness theorem to unconditional kernels and states that conditional completeness needs a new hedge analogue.

seed_details.anchor_location: Example B.6; Algorithm 3; concluding conditional-completeness paragraph.
seed_details.kernel: Either Branch-sCIDP is complete, or there is a bounded-size selected COPAG whose all-branches-fail query is nevertheless identified; characterize the smallest obstruction and the failed forest property.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the global represented-MAG construction by finite obstruction extraction under graph minors and role-state quotients.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for minimal sCIDP counterexamples and selected PAG conditional obstructions found no source beyond the explicit open problem.
seed_details.red_team: This is only a computational search over tiny graphs.
seed_details.rebuttal: A publishable version requires a finite-obstruction theorem or a smallest semantic counterexample, not enumeration alone.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; Theorem 5.1 and proof; Algorithms 1--2; Theorem 6.1; Sections 7.2--7.3; Conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: A support-aware Branch-sCIDP returns the maximal observed-law domain on which a selected conditional effect is point identified, with an if-and-only-if support certificate across all represented MAGs.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Hwang's topological-order positivity propagation must be made invariant across represented MAGs and through selected Rule-2 role states.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining positivity-aware CIDP, selected PAGs, and maximal support found fixed-graph positivity results but no selected equivalence-class theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by running Hwang's positivity algorithm on each represented MAG.
seed_details.rebuttal: Enumeration is exponential, support conditions can disagree across representatives, and selection changes the conditional kernels whose denominators must be licensed.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; lower- and upper-bound propositions; Partial IDP algorithm; discussion of unknown tightness; Conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: The sharp identified interval for a positive discrete selected conditional PAG query is the extrema of one graph-indexed fractional polynomial program, with endpoint model certificates across the represented class.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Bellot's analytic PAG decomposition must incorporate selected-law constraints and couple numerator and denominator before proving endpoint sharpness over the union of represented selected graphs.
seed_details.destination_search: Bellot omits selection; Duarte and coauthors handle selection for a specified discrete causal model but not the PAG-represented union.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Duarte's generic polynomial-program reduction.
seed_details.rebuttal: Duarte's input is a fixed causal specification; a graph-native reduction over every selected MAG represented by a PAG and a sharp union certificate are absent.

seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction; regime-indicator causal-calculus construction; generalized ID algorithm and its explicit no-completeness remark; Conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: Conditional identification in iCOPAGs is complete if and only if exhaustive input-aware role branching succeeds, with failure preserving every input-indexed selected observational kernel.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The witness pair must preserve a family of transitional kernels indexed by inputs rather than one selected observational law.
seed_details.destination_search: Input-aware ioSCM calculi and selected iSOPAG soundness were located, but no equivalence-class conditional converse.
seed_details.red_team: Inputs are syntactic labels, so the input-free proof lifts verbatim.
seed_details.rebuttal: Input kernels add observational constraints across regimes, and the existing represented-forest pair is not shown to preserve them jointly.

seed_details.anchor_location: Concluding paragraph on efficiency and discover-then-estimate inference; Algorithm 3 normalization.
seed_details.kernel: For every fixed successful sCIDP formula, derive the efficient influence function of its normalized selected conditional value and construct an attaining cross-fitted estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the selected assembly-tree functional jointly in numerator and denominator and control quotient remainders near the maintained positivity boundary.
seed_details.destination_search: PAG-DML covers identified PAG functionals without this selected conditional normalization; no selected sCIDP efficiency bound was found.
seed_details.red_team: The quotient rule makes the influence function routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The derivative of a fixed quotient is routine, but recursively differentiating the selected assembly tree and proving efficiency and product-rate control are not supplied by the graphical paper.

seed_details.anchor_location: Concluding paragraph on discover-then-estimate pipelines and latent selection.
seed_details.kernel: A resampling-and-screening confidence set unions normalized functionals over nonrejected selected PAGs and branches and covers the fixed selected causal target after FCI.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The post-discovery screening event must control PAG edge marks, latent-selection equivalence classes, and discontinuous branch changes simultaneously.
seed_details.destination_search: Current post-discovery coverage results center on PC and DAG adjustment; no selected FCI/PAG branch-union theorem was found.
seed_details.red_team: Take a union over all PAGs and coverage is automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: An unrestricted union is vacuous; useful coverage requires a screened graph set and uniform control of formula and branch selection.

seed_details.anchor_location: Proof of Theorem 4.15 and selected-forest nonidentifiability construction.
seed_details.kernel: Every unconditional sIDP failure on a binary COPAG compiles to an explicit positive rational binary SCM pair with polynomial verification in expanded certificate size.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace existential positive countermodels by a rational interior parameterization and exact arithmetic certificate.
seed_details.destination_search: The source proves semantic nonidentifiability but does not advertise rational witness synthesis or certificate complexity.
seed_details.red_team: Density of rationals makes the compilation immediate.
seed_details.rebuttal: Approximation does not preserve exact observational equality; a rational algebraic construction is required.

seed_details.anchor_location: Conclusion, paragraph proposing early stopping in the FCI--identification pipeline.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize the earliest partially oriented FCI state at which a selected conditional effect has an invariant Branch-sCIDP formula, and certify persistence under every later orientation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The separation and region arguments must become monotone under shrinking represented-graph classes along the FCI orientation sequence.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for early-stopping FCI conditional identification under selection found the source's open direction but no theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Run identification after each FCI rule and stop at the first success.
seed_details.rebuttal: A sound stopping rule needs persistence of the formula over all completions and later orientations, not merely success on one transient partial graph.

seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 5.1 and proof; Theorem 6.1; discussion of positivity-aware projection and conditional causal effects; Conclusion.
seed_details.kernel: For a fixed successful selected-PAG conditional formula, derive a necessary-and-sufficient observed-law support condition licensing every division and Rule-2 exchange, and prove maximality of its evaluation domain.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The fixed-graph c-factor positivity propagation must be lifted to all represented selected graphs and to the terminal normalization denominator.
seed_details.destination_search: No positivity-aware CIDP or sCIDP theorem under latent selection and Markov equivalence was located.
